source.title: AdaBelief Optimizer: Adapting Stepsizes by the Belief in Observed Gradients
source.authors: Juntang Zhuang; Tommy M. Tang; Yifan Ding; S. Tatikonda; N. Dvornek; X. Papademetris; J. Duncan

record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out image and language benchmarks, using different optimizer methods and measures from the original optimizer studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out results for natural-label tasks. Its discussion of generalization gaps in prior work is background, not this study's result. GAN FID and reinforcement-learning reward do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares an adaptive optimizer, AdaBelief, with SGD using held-out image-classification accuracy and language-model perplexity. Its own results bear on V4, although tuning extends beyond learning rates and schedules. Most other ImageNet optimizer results are imported from earlier papers.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that AdaBelief combines fast convergence, generalization comparable to SGD, and training stability, citing comparable ImageNet accuracy, better CIFAR accuracy, strong language-model results, and GAN experiments.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces AdaBelief, an Adam modification using an EMA of squared deviations between observed and averaged gradients; compares it with SGD and other optimizers on standard datasets.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported performance varies by task and model depth: AdaBelief is close to other optimizers on 1-layer LSTM and lowest in test perplexity on 2- and 3-layer LSTMs. CIFAR experiments use extensive optimizer hyperparameter searches; ImageNet comparisons use AdaBelief's Adam defaults and literature results for other optimizers.

fits_no_version.finding: AdaBelief has a smaller training-test accuracy gap than optimizers such as Yogi.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects the training-test accuracy gap on CIFAR classifiers.

record.problems: ImageNet comparison is not an extensive hyperparameter search and compares AdaBelief with other optimizers' best literature results. Several relevant CIFAR, LSTM, and train-test-gap outcomes are figure-only in the supplied text, without recoverable numeric values. Training accuracy values are not provided in text for calculating gaps.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant reported result rows omitted. Other optimizer table entries for ImageNet are included only when they bear on the adaptive-method versus SGD comparison; GAN FID, translation BLEU, object detection mAP and reinforcement-learning reward do not test the listed versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width-dependent test error beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

A controlled comparison restricted to learning-rate and schedule tuning; a controlled limited-versus-broader-tuning intervention; isolated recovery through decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD; numerical confirmation of equal or better training performance accompanying worse held-out performance. Word-level language modeling is tested.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and augmentation interactions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: No supports verdict is warranted from R2–R7 because those ImageNet comparisons are imported results. The supplied text contains figure captions and qualitative summaries but no readable plotted values; architecture-specific effect sizes and SGD-specific perplexity differences cannot be recovered. Comparisons between adaptive optimizers alone do not establish V4's adaptive-versus-SGD pattern.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Broader tuning, decoupled weight decay as a recovery method, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Train with AdaBelief and evaluate validation top-1 accuracy.
rows.note: Authors describe AdaBelief's accuracy as comparable to SGD.
rows.check: AdaBelief's 70.08% versus SGD's 70.23% is explicitly described as comparable, so an adaptive-optimizer disadvantage is absent. The SGD table value is cited from earlier work; Appendix F.2 also reports an own-run comparison. AdaBelief uses decoupled weight decay and a different decay schedule.

rows.note: The two cited Adam values are reported parenthetically as printed.
rows.check: Both Adam values and the SGD baseline are cited results, not this study's measurements. Remove from the study's own-result rows or mark as cited context; do not base its verdict on them.

rows.subject: VGG11, ResNet34 and DenseNet121
rows.operation_detail: Compare optimizers on CIFAR test accuracy; figure values only.

conditions.value: AdaBelief versus SGD and other methods

rows.uncertainty: [µ ± σ] across 3 runs, stated for CIFAR experiments
rows.locator: Figure 4; Section 3, CNNs on image classification
rows.note: Text says AdaBelief achieves better accuracy than SGD and other methods. Separate model and dataset values cannot be recovered from the supplied figure text.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports better accuracy for AdaBelief than SGD. Split into six architecture-by-dataset rows when figure values are available. Tuning includes momentum parameters and, for AdamW, weight decay, so this does not reproduce V4's limited-tuning condition.

rows.subject: 1-layer LSTM
rows.operation_detail: Compare optimizer test perplexity; figure values only.
rows.note: Text says performance is close to other optimizers for the 1-layer model.
rows.check: The authors describe AdaBelief as close to other optimizers, not partially worse. Record an explicit SGD comparator when the figure is available. This is word-level language modeling; the 1-layer AdaBelief recipe uses epsilon 10^-12 rather than the default 10^-8.

rows.subject: 2-layer LSTM
rows.operation_detail: Compare optimizer test perplexity; figure values only.
rows.note: Text says AdaBelief achieves the lowest perplexity for 2-layer models.
rows.check: Lowest test perplexity means the adaptive optimizer performs better, reversing the disadvantage rather than observing it. Record the SGD-specific comparison from the figure; numeric differences are unavailable in the supplied text.

rows.subject: 3-layer LSTM
rows.operation_detail: Compare optimizer test perplexity; figure values only.
rows.note: Text says AdaBelief achieves the lowest perplexity for 3-layer models.
rows.check: Lowest test perplexity means the adaptive optimizer performs better, reversing the disadvantage rather than observing it. Record the SGD-specific comparison from the figure; numeric differences are unavailable in the supplied text.

rows.subject: VGG11, ResNet34 and DenseNet121
rows.operation_detail: Compare training-test accuracy gap across optimizers; figure values only.

conditions.value: AdaBelief versus other optimizers, including Yogi

rows.measure: gap between training and test accuracy
rows.uncertainty: confidence interval [µ ± σ] of 3 independent runs
rows.note: Text says AdaBelief has a smaller gap than other optimizers such as Yogi; model-specific values are not available in the supplied figure text.
rows.check: A smaller training-test accuracy gap relative to Yogi does not establish adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance. It also measures neither sharpness nor sharpness-gap correlation, so it does not test V7.

relationships.condition: ResNet18 on ImageNet with AdaBelief, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer-specific learning-rate schedules
relationships.reason: R1 reports 70.08% versus SGD's 70.23%, explicitly described as comparable; this adaptive-method exception depends on the tested optimizer and recipe.
relationships.display_finding: AdaBelief reportedly achieved accuracy comparable to SGD, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: VGG11, ResNet34, and DenseNet121 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 with broader optimizer tuning
relationships.reason: The text accompanying R8 reports AdaBelief outperforming SGD; the search includes parameters beyond learning rates and schedules, qualifying the adaptive-method disadvantage.
relationships.display_finding: Broader optimizer searches reportedly yielded an AdaBelief advantage over SGD, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.reason: The text accompanying R9 reports comparable performance across optimizers, providing no adaptive disadvantage in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: The optimizers reportedly performed comparably, but this result remains unverified.

relationships.condition: 2-layer and 3-layer word-level LSTMs on Penn Treebank
relationships.reason: The text accompanying R10 and R11 reports the lowest test perplexity for AdaBelief, showing that the adaptive-method disadvantage does not extend to these optimizer-model combinations.
relationships.display_finding: AdaBelief reportedly achieved the lowest test perplexity, but these results remain unverified.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: AdaBelief on ImageNet, CIFAR image classification, and Penn TreeBank LSTMs
reader_labels.reason: AdaBelief is comparable to SGD on ImageNet, outperforms the compared optimizers on CIFAR, and performs close to or better than other optimizers on LSTMs, so the adaptive-method pattern depends on the method and setting (R1, R8–R11).
